The '''2005 Tippeligaen''' was the 61st completed season of top division [[association football|football]] in [[Norway]]. The season began on 10 April 2005, and was concluded with the last of 26 rounds played on 29 October. 3 points were given for wins and 1 for draws.

[[Vålerenga Fotball|Vålerenga]], the winner of this year's season entered the second round of next year's [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] qualification, while the runners-up ([[IK Start|Start]]), number 3 ([[FK Lyn|Lyn]]) and the [[Norwegian Cup]] winners enter the [[UEFA Cup]] qualification round. The top four teams qualified for the [[2004–05 Royal League]].

1,726,145 people attended the matches, a new record for the Tippeligaen and 300,000 more than the previous year. It is also more than twice as many as in 1995, when only 841,717 attended the matches during the whole season. The 2005 season was, as of 2019, the last season where all the teams in the division played on natural turfs only.

==Overview==
===Summary===
The greatest surprises of the 2005 season were the great performance of Start, promoted to the Tippeligaen in the [[2004 Tippeligaen|2004 season]] and ended up winning silver, and the disappointing performance of [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] which fought against relegation from the top division after winning it for 13 straight seasons.

The season ended on a sad note as [[Fredrikstad FK|Fredrikstad]]'s [[Dagfinn Enerly]] got a serious neck injury in the last round match against Start on 29 October 2005, which made him a [[paraplegic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nrk.no/ostfold/enerly-brakk-nakken-1.347297 |title=Enerly brakk nakken |website=www.nrk.no |publisher=NRK |language=no |date=30 October 2005 |access-date=22 May 2019}}</ref> Start lost the game 1–3 which meant that Vålerenga secured their fifth league title with a 2–2 draw against [[Odd Grenland]] in [[Skien (town)|Skien]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dagbladet.no/sport/valerenga-er-seriemestere/66148357 |title=Vålerenga er seriemestere |trans-title=Vålerenga are league champions |website=www.dagbladet.no |publisher=[[Dagbladet]] |language=no |date=29 October 2005 |access-date=22 May 2019}}</ref>

Number thirteen ([[Aalesunds FK|Aalesund]]) and fourteen ([[FK Bodø/Glimt|Bodø/Glimt]]) were relegated to [[2006 1. divisjon|1. divisjon]], while number twelve ([[Molde FK|Molde]]) had to play a two-legged play-off (home and away) against [[Moss FK|Moss]], third-place finisher in [[Adeccoligaen]], for the last spot in next year's season. Molde won the play-off matches 5–2 on aggregate and remained in Tippeligaen.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.vg.no/sport/fotball/i/ngR9qm/molde-reddet-plassen |title=Molde reddet plassen |website=www.vg.no |publisher=[[Verdens Gang]] |language=no |date=19 November 2005 |access-date=22 May 2019}}</ref>

==Teams and locations==
Fourteen teams competed in the league – the top twelve teams from the previous season, and two teams promoted from [[2004 1. divisjon|1. divisjon]].
